## Fixed

- **Automatic backups never started on Linux.** The systemd timer was
  written with a trigger that counts from the last time the backup ran
  — so on a machine where it had never run, there was nothing to count
  from and it never fired at all. If you installed r2backup on Linux and
  scheduled it, it has been sitting there doing nothing. Upgrading
  rewrites the timer; nothing to do by hand. macOS and Windows were
  never affected.

- **One copy of r2b stopped the others working.** The index takes an
  exclusive lock while it is open, and the window held that lock for as
  long as it was on screen — so a scheduled backup, or `r2b status`, or
  `r2b ls`, would wait five seconds and fail while a window sat idle
  with nobody doing anything in it. The window now takes the lock only
  while it is actually reading or writing, and lets go in between.
  `r2b status --watch` opened the index for no reason at all, which
  meant the one command whose whole purpose is following a running
  backup was the one command guaranteed to fail during one; it opens
  nothing now. And when something genuinely is holding the lock, the
  message says another copy of r2b is running, instead of `timeout`.

- **A backup you stopped was recorded as one that finished.** Pressing
  q partway through wrote a clean entry: `status` and the folder list
  showed "no changes" for a run that was cut off. They say "cancelled"
  now — and a run you stopped on purpose is no longer coloured and
  worded as a failure.

- **Removing a folder left uploads running up a bill.** A file
  interrupted partway leaves its uploaded parts on the server. Removing
  the folder forgot about them locally without telling R2, so they kept
  being charged for, with no file in any listing to explain the charge,
  and nothing left that could find them again. Removal now stops them on
  the server first, and says how many it stopped. `--purge` also asks
  the bucket directly, which catches ones your computer never knew
  about.

- **A mistyped secret key could not be corrected without restarting.**
  Fixing it in the same window saved the new key and then tested the old
  one, failing exactly the same way, until you quit and reopened r2b.

- **Every device in your account was dated 1 January 1970.**

- **The help overlay could not tell you how to close it.** It laid out
  in seven columns and quietly dropped the ones that did not fit — which
  included the column holding Quit and Help. It is two columns now, and
  everything fits at 80.

- **Trash said every file was deleted at 00:00.** The real time was in
  the record all along. Where there genuinely is no time — a file
  something else put in the trash tree — it shows the date alone rather
  than inventing one.

- **A renamed folder showed up twice.** Renaming changes only what this
  computer calls a folder; the bucket keeps its original name. The
  Folders tab compared the two by name, so after a rename your own
  backup came back looking like an unclaimed one belonging to nobody,
  sitting next to itself under its new name.

- **`rename` now tells you the name other computers still need.** That
  original name is the only one `restore` works under anywhere else, and
  nothing said so.

- **Repairing a schedule failed on machines whose scheduler cannot say
  how often it runs** — which is the crontab fallback, and some Windows
  setups. The installer runs a repair right after replacing files, so
  this landed on exactly the unattended path that must not fail.

- **The month's operation count charged for uploads that failed.** It
  counted what a run planned to do rather than what it did, so the
  number claimed you had less of the free tier left than you had
  actually spent.

- **A folder being backed up right now cannot be removed** — from the
  window or the command line. Doing it mid-run made the index forget
  everything uploaded before the removal.

- **`edit` says it is about to back up.** It always did back up, so the
  change takes effect; it just did not mention that it was about to
  spend operations and start a transfer.

- **The command line writes intervals the way you would say them** —
  "every 30 minutes", not "every 30m0s". The window already did.

- **On the running screen, q says what it does:** it stops the run *and*
  quits. Read next to esc, "q stops it" invited the idea that it was a
  way to leave the backup going.

- **Setup names what is protecting your keys on both paths in** — typed
  by hand, or pulled from your account on a second computer.

- **"Costs nothing when nothing changed" was very nearly true.** Once a
  day, the first run after midnight UTC also spends one request expiring
  trash that has aged out, for a folder with retention turned on.
  `r2b backup` now prints that count instead of a hardcoded zero.

## Heads up

- **On macOS and Linux, your secret key is protected by file
  permissions, not by an OS keystore.** That has always been the case —
  only Windows has a keystore backend (DPAPI) — but the documentation
  claimed Keychain and libsecret support that was never written. What
  r2b told you on screen at setup was always accurate; what was written
  down about it was not.
